qt: to the Commission Marco Falcone (PPE), Caterina Chinnici (PPE), Salvatore De Meo (PPE), Letizia Moratti (PPE), Fulvio Martusciello (PPE), Giusi Princi (PPE), Massimiliano Salini (PPE), Flavio Tosi (PPE), Herbert Dorfmann (PPE) Subject:

On the night of 1 to 2 November, hackers took over a number of supermarket fridges and freezers in Italy and eight other Member States, setting the temperatures as high as 50 degrees Celsius. These attacks compromised vast quantities of food, which had to be withdrawn as a result. The Commission has denounced what it calls a ‘deliberate attempt to disrupt food supply chains’. This episode shows just how vulnerable the technological infrastructure that supports the distribution of basic necessities is, seeing as a single cyber-attack can meaningfully threaten the food security and supply chain continuity that citizens and businesses alike rely on. In the light of the above, we ask the Commission: 1.

What information has it gathered on the people and entities behind these attacks, and what steps will it take to ensure a coordinated European response that includes holding any responsible hostile states to account?

What instruments will it deploy to fund efforts by retailers and major operators in this sector to upgrade and update their IT security systems so that businesses, particularly smaller ones, do not have to bear the costs involved alone?
Will it make use of European resources and financial instruments to compensate the businesses affected and fund efforts to make these facilities safe from future attacks?
